description.value: The Port McNeill & District Museum is a community-built institution dedicated to logging memorabilia from British Columbia's North Island, opened in 2000. It features video exhibits including 'The Last Logging Railway in North America' and 'Women in Log Scaling,' offering a compelling look at the industrial heritage of the region. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible cultural detour for cyclists exploring the northern tip of Vancouver Island.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content for portmcneill.ca/residents/museum/ clearly describes the Port McNeill & District Museum as a community-built logging memorabilia museum opened in 2000. The site states it is 'Open by appointment,' which is an important qualifier. No cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, water, washrooms) are mentioned anywhere on the website or in the OSM tags, so all amenity fields default to null. Phone (250-956-3881) and mailing address (Box 1179, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0) are drawn from the website, as OSM records both as empty.
concerns: Museum is listed as 'Open by appointment' on the website — cyclists cannot assume walk-in access without calling ahead.
The HTML page title reads 'Alert Bay BC | Museum' despite the museum being located in Port McNeill; likely a website metadata error.
Only a mailing/PO Box address (Box 1179) is provided — no physical street address is listed on the website or in OSM.
OSM had no phone or address for this record; both were sourced from the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, operating community museum and a named tourism stop on the North Island route; relevant as a cultural attraction for touring cyclists passing through Port McNeill. Appointment-only access should be noted so cyclists can plan ahead.

wow_evidence: Small community museum of North Island logging memorabilia; by-donation; video exhibits incl. last logging railway in North America.
blurb: Logging-history museum; by donation; last logging railway in North America footage.
